body:
`ColumnReader::block`, the buffer holding each page's decompressed data, was previously allocated with an `Allocator` and was always kept pinned.

This moves `block` onto the buffer manager (`BlockHandle`/`BufferHandle`), pinning it only around each vector's read and unpinning it in between. `ByteBuffer` was changed to use an offset-based cursor instead of an absolute pointer. Further, every decoder that caches a pointer into `block` (dictionary, RLE, delta-binary-packed, byte-stream-split) now rebases itself against the new address after each re-pin.

One buffer was deliberately left on `Allocator`: the bloom filter built while writing a dictionary page. It's short-lived and never re-pinned, so buffer-manager tracking would only add overhead there with no eviction benefit.

I ran a small benchmark locally, no speed regression, and it now keeps working once memory gets tight enough that main just runs out of memory.

Also includes a small unrelated build fix in `expression_binder.cpp` I hit along the way.

This looks like a lot of changes, but a lot of the changes are because many of the functions were renamed for formatting reasons (ie. `inc()` -> `Inc()`).

Hi @lnkuiper, thanks for the pointers on the regressions. I implemented your proposed changes but a benchmark after revealed that most of the slowdown was actually somewhere else, and I actually went through several iterations to try and narrow it down:

| | before patch suggestion | with patch + scratch-buffer extensions ([`1844327`](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/commit/1844327b8bc)) | + pow2 alloc fix ([`6ed74be`](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/commit/6ed74be19a5)) | final, + eviction-queue skip ([`0b6f445`](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/commit/0b6f445880b)) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| geomean | 2–4% (your Codex run) | +2.1% | +2.4% | **+0.3–1.2%** (4 runs) |
| q13 (worst) | — | +9.6% | +1.3% | within ±3% |
| q13 page faults/run | — | ~23k | ~3.5k | ~3.5k |

The leftover slowdown is the per-vector pin/unpin itself, so there's no real workaround without holding pins longer.

review_comments.body: This seems a bit error-prone - if we forget to call this rebase we run into issues. Would it be possible for the decoders to instead refer to the block and get the pointer from there instead of storing one?

Doing it via block directly would mean every `Read()`/`Skip()` in these decode loops resolves the pointer through an extra indirection instead of a direct dereference. I could add an extra `D_ASSERT` instead to catch a missing `Rebase()`?

Maybe the pointer can instead be resolved on `Pin()` instead of being kept around in these decoders?

I'm just a bit worried about caching these pointers as the current code looks rather fragile - it seems easy to forget calling a `Rebase()` or to forget calling a `Pin()` only to be hit with crashes, and I would prefer if the code would protect against this directly.
Instead of having to remember to `Pin / Unpin` can we use an object with a destructor similar to our buffer manager (a `BufferHandle` like object).

title: Allow Pinning/Unpinning of ColumnReader::block
